mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC rose monotonically from -25.4 to -22.0 across the four weeks ending 2020-08-15. This trend momentum persists because the reopening sequence that produced it is still in force, lifting the next 28-day mean above the trailing 28-day mean of -23.4.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly means rose from -25.4 at t-3w to -22.0 at t-0w, a gain of 3.4 points
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is at or below -23.4, meaning the series fails to gain on its own trailing four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS jumped 7.0 points in the final week (-18.9 to -11.9), well outside its 2-point weekly variation. Households substituting outdoor recreation for indoor discretionary shopping divert spend away from malls, pulling RETAIL_REC down over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -18.9 at t-1w to -11.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: In the two weeks following a greater-than-5-point weekly PARKS rise, the mean of RETAIL_REC is higher than in the two weeks preceding that rise.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are jointly depressed and have never left the -24 to -36 band in any snapshot week. The weekday commuter and lunchtime footfall that anchors urban retail stays absent while both series sit at these levels, so RETAIL_REC cannot escape its -22 to -25 range over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -30.1 and TRANSIT at -33.7 at t-0w, both below -30
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC registers a higher 28-day forward mean while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain at or below -30 for the entire forward window.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT sits at or below -30, occupancy caps and capacity limits on malls bind, and RETAIL_REC is mechanically pinned in a -20 to -25 channel. Under that regime the forward 28-day mean stays below the trailing mean of -23.4.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT at or below -30 for two or more consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed between -36.4 and -33.0 in all four snapshot weeks
regime_hint: restrictions in force with TRANSIT at or below -30
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds -23.4 while TRANSIT remains at or below -30 throughout that window.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has fallen back to -2.3 from +0.1 two weeks earlier, showing the stockpiling phase is over. As grocery trip frequency normalises, household attention rotates back to discretionary retail, lifting RETAIL_REC within the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM prints below 0 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from 0.1 at t-2w to -2.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: In the week following two consecutive sub-zero GROCERY_PHARM prints, RETAIL_REC does not exceed its -22.0 level of t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has declined from 22.4 to 19.9 over four weeks, meaning less time is spent at home. Every further drop in RESIDENTIAL translates into additional out-of-home discretionary trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 22.4 at t-3w to 19.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is below -23.4 even though RESIDENTIAL continues to fall below its t-0w level.

mechanism_narrative: The window from mid-August to mid-September marks the late-Q3 discretionary retail build in Singapore. The seasonal spending cycle alone lifts RETAIL_REC above its trailing four-week mean, independent of any restriction change.
evidence_refs: fact:decision point 2020-08-15 sits at the start of the late-Q3 retail build window
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is at or below -23.4, showing no seasonal uplift above the trailing mean.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES fell 5.8 points in the final week (-24.3 to -30.1), a reversal consistent with renewed work-from-home guidance. The lost weekday commuter base removes a core retail demand pool and suppresses RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped from -24.3 at t-1w to -30.1 at t-0w while TRANSIT stayed at -33.7
failure_condition: Following a greater-than-5-point weekly WORKPLACES drop, the two-week forward mean of RETAIL_REC is higher than its -22.05 mean over t-1w and t-0w.
